name: Cartouche
subtitle: Cartouche itself
description: The source Cartouche's built-in SideStore reads for Cartouche's own updates. It lists Cartouche and nothing else: Cartouche never lists, hosts or downloads games.

apps.name: Cartouche
apps.subtitle: Play your own games built with nxnative
apps.localizedDescription: Cartouche runs the games you build with nxnative from your own copies, renews itself without a computer, and gives them Increased Memory Limit. It never downloads a game.

versions.localizedDescription:
Cartouche offers to update a game when your games folder holds a newer build of it.

- Games: when your games folder holds a newer IPA of a game you installed, a later version of the game, or the same version built again from a newer nxnative, such as one Cartouche Builder made, the console shows Update for the game and a badge on its cartridge, and its sheet Update from your games folder. The game's settings and saves stay.
- Games: a game's sheet shows which build of it is on this iPhone, and the newer one in your games folder: its version, the nxnative commit it was built from and when it was built.
- Games: a copy Cartouche writes of a game to your games folder keeps when the game was built, so that it is never offered as an update over the same game.

Games install from your storage again, and the icon keeps no badge.

- Install: a game whose IPA holds a large deflated file, such as a RomFS image of several GB, installs from your shared folder, S3 bucket or server. Cartouche stopped with "romfs.img is damaged (its deflated data ends early)": the end of the file was never decoded.
- Icon: Cartouche's icon no longer shows a badge with nothing behind it. The built-in SideStore counted the available updates there and never took the count away; Cartouche clears it when it opens.

Your games and saves on an SFTP server of yours.

- Storage: System › Storage › Add an SFTP server reaches a server of yours, such as your NAS's or your Mac's, with your account on it. Your games folder and saves folder can be there, as on a shared folder.
- Storage: Cartouche keeps the server's key when you save it and shows its fingerprint. Should the server show another key later, Cartouche stops before sending your password; if you reinstalled the server, remove it in Cartouche and add it again. Your password stays in this iPhone's keychain.

Your games and saves on an FTP server of yours.

- Storage: System › Storage › Add an FTP server reaches a server of your network, such as your NAS's, with your account on it. Your games folder and saves folder can be there, as on a shared folder.
- Storage: FTP sends your password unencrypted, so use it on your own network. Cartouche keeps the password in this iPhone's keychain.

Your games and saves on an S3 bucket of yours.

- Storage: System › Storage › Add S3 storage reaches a private bucket on Amazon S3, or on a server of your own such as MinIO on your NAS, with your access key. Your games folder and saves folder can be there, as on a shared folder.
- Storage: every request is signed with your keys, and the secret key stays in this iPhone's keychain. Cartouche reaches no public bucket.
- Storage: type http:// before the address of a server on your network without HTTPS; Cartouche uses HTTPS otherwise.

Signing in again finds the certificate the Cartouche Installer left.

- Setup: after an install with the Cartouche Installer that revoked the old certificate, signing in again stopped with "This Apple account already has a certificate". The built-in SideStore now finds the installer's certificate however its serial number is written, and otherwise looks for it in every key file Cartouche holds.
- Setup: should it still not find one, the message says which certificate Cartouche names and which ones your account has.
- Install this version with the Cartouche Installer if games do not start: Cartouche offers no update while its certificate does not work.

Games start again after an install from another computer.

- Games: when the Cartouche Installer, run from another computer, revoked the old certificate, games no longer started ("the app is signed with the latest certificate but its signature is invalid"). Cartouche now checks that iOS accepts the certificate games are signed with, and if not, signs in again with your Apple ID by itself to take the new one. It asks you only should Apple want a verification code.
- Updates: Cartouche offers none while its certificate does not work, since an update signed with a revoked certificate would not open.
- Install this version with the Cartouche Installer if a game shows that message: an update from inside Cartouche would be signed with the revoked certificate.

Updates from inside Cartouche, and storage that copes with large games and read-only shared folders.

- Updates: Cartouche looks for its new versions itself, when it opens and when you come back to it, and offers them over the console with Update and Later. The System page shows them too, with what's new, and Check for an update. The built-in SideStore installs the new version without a computer and without showing itself, with LocalDevVPN connected, then Cartouche goes to the home screen for iOS to install it: open it again. Your games and their saves stay.
- This is the first version that updates itself: install it once with the Cartouche Installer, over the Cartouche you have. The next ones come from inside Cartouche.
- Storage: copying a large game to your storage, such as Mario Kart World to a NAS, no longer closes Cartouche partway through.
- Storage: a shared folder your account can only read shows as read-only. Its games still install, but it takes no saves and no copy of a game.

Your own storage, the games' covers, and Cartouche's screens only.

- Storage: keep your games and your saves on a shared folder of your Mac, PC or NAS (SMB), or on a folder in Files, with your own account. Set it up in System, Storage; the password stays in this iPhone's keychain.
- The games in your games folder show in All games with Install from: Cartouche unpacks the IPA as it arrives, so the iPhone never holds both. Copy to puts an installed game there as an IPA, and Uninstall offers to copy it first.
- Each IPA there goes to its game by itself, by the game's title ID: the one nxnative writes in the IPA, or one in the file's name. An IPA iCloud Drive keeps online only goes by its name, such as MarioKartWorld-nxnative-6nov-v2.ipa, until it is downloaded.
- Your saves are copied to your saves folder after each game, the ten newest kept. A game's details list the copies and put one back.
- Covers: every game shows its official cover from IGDB, whole, on a label shaped like a game case, and its artwork behind its details. All 138 games have one.
- Cartouche shows only its own screens: LiveContainer's Apps and Settings tabs, the Open SideStore button and the app's page in the Settings app are gone. System opens over the console from the dock or the controller's Menu button, and OK or Menu closes it.
- The dock stays at the bottom, the shelves scrolling under it. From iOS 18, a game's details grow out of its cartridge.
- Game settings show one of nxnative's sections at a time, picked on a row of buttons or with L and R, the cloud saves last.
- The Mac filter also lists the games nxnative plays on the iPhone, which it plays on the Mac too.

A console's home, for every iPhone and the iPhone Duo.

- Home: your games on the first shelf and the games nxnative plays on the iPhone on the second, as cartridges. The game in focus shows under them with Play, or Import my copy, and its details. A dock leads to All games, Import, System, Apps and Settings.
- All games: every game of nxnative's list, 138 today, filtered by where nxnative plays it (iPhone, Mac, bring-up) or Switch 2, and searched by name or title ID.
- A game controller drives every screen: the D-pad moves, A plays, X opens a game's details, B goes back, L and R change the filter.
- iPhone Duo: Cartouche now uses the whole display, built with the iOS 27.2 SDK; larger cartridges unfolded, the shelves beside the game in focus when held sideways, details as a card.
- A game's details say what nxnative says of it: where it plays it, the engine, the game version and SDK of its profile, its title ID and other regions.
- Games install in Cartouche: Import my copy unpacks and signs the IPA over the console, with its progress, then opens the game's details with Play. The Apps tab no longer shows. An IPA of a game you have replaces it and keeps your saves.
- Play starts the game at once, without nxnative's settings screen.
- Game settings, in a game's details: the settings of nxnative's screen in Cartouche, in French (frame rate, render scale, console mode, language, rumble, cloud saves and the rest), saved where the game reads them. Start on nxnative's screen is still there.
- Uninstall, from a game's details or a long press on it, keeping your saves for the next import or erasing them.
